When validating an array element, the internal call to `atPath(currentPath, index)` should correctly build the JSON‑Pointer path (e.g., `/items/0`). The test verifies that no exception is thrown and the path is used in any generated messages.

When validating a nested object property, the call to `atPath(currentPath, token)` must correctly concatenate the token (e.g., `/address/street`). The test checks that the generated message (if any) contains the expected path.

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage with messageId='required' from the referenced sub‑schema
cases.description: `suppressSubSchemaRetrieval` is false. The validator's `schemaNode` contains a `$ref` that resolves to a sub‑schema requiring property `id`. The instance object does not contain `id`. The validator must fetch the sub‑schema via `fetchSubSchemaNode`, apply its rules and return a `required` validation message.

`suppressSubSchemaRetrieval` is false but `fetchSubSchemaNode` returns `null` (no `$ref` present). The current schema only checks that the node is an object, which it is, so validation succeeds with no messages.

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage with messageId='minimum'

cases.description: Using the same numeric schema, the node value is 10 which equals the `exclusiveMaximum`. Because the maximum is exclusive, validation must fail with an `exclusiveMaximum` message.

The validator must build the correct JSON‑Pointer path using successive `atPath` calls and report the `required` message with the full path `/level1/level2/missingProp`.
